Subject: General

Topic 3.2: Writing readiness (a-e)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing readiness (a-e), part of Writing 3.1 Eye-hand co- ordination By the end of the sub strand, the learner sh in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we hold our pencils or pens when writing? 2. Where do we write on?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing readiness (a-e) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: Writing readiness as the learner joins dots of letter sounds from left to right on their

books filling each page from top to bottom.

• Creativity and imagination: Originality as the learner models letter sounds for mastery using modelling clay

Values:
• Peace. Inner peace is enhanced as the learner develops tolerance and take time to join dots.

• Integrity is developed as the learner tries best to write letters on their own and not let anybody else do it even when it seems

challenging.

35

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental conservation awareness where the learner learns that even as we learn to write, not every surface is a writing

material (walls, clothes).

Link to other Learning Areas: All learning areas as the learner writes during different activities.

Suggested learning resources: Clay, plasticine or dough, book, colour pencil
